#3093. Warhammer Survivors Isn’t Much More Than a Vampire Survivors Reskin, Which Is (Mostly) OK

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Though it passes up the opportunity to move the genre into new territory, the game is a tasty, if familiar, piece of gaming junk food.

When I first heard that developers Auroch Digital and Vampire Survivors creator Luca “Poncle” Galante were working together on Warhammer Survivors, I was thrilled. A studio of Warhammer lore fiends collaborating with a solo dev who birthed a genre seemed like a recipe for success.

But having now played through most of the game’s sci-fi battles and a smattering of fantasy incursions, I think your enjoyment of this game probably hinges entirely on how many modern bullet heaven games you’ve played. If you’re looking for something that meaningfully changes the formula, you won’t find it here.

While Vampire Survivors should be respected and lauded for laying the foundations for an entirely new type of video game, it has been surpassed by newer projects that have fundamentally changed the fledgling bullet heaven genre for the better. Newer games have implemented incredibly robust progression systems, more objective-based gameplay and entirely new camera perspectives.

There’s no problem with Survivors being knocked off the pedestal it built – every developer should learn from their peers, and the oldest games will never be the most polished games (even if they stand the test of time as cult classics).

The issue is that Warhammer Survivors just feels like a massive, reskinned expansion of Poncle’s original game. Despite a striking visual identity and plenty of Warhammer-themed weapons and items, this game never escapes the shadow of Vampire Survivors, which may diminish the enjoyment of genre enthusiasts.

Auroch Digital’s stab at a bullet heaven game isn’t unique, and its thrills wear out sooner than one might expect, but I think that’s mostly OK. It’s full of charming, vibrant Warhammer-themed pixel art, and that feels like what the true appeal of Warhammer Survivors just might be. This is the type of video game junk food that keeps you up until 5 a.m. every once in a while, completely destroying your sleep schedule. It won’t go down as one of the bullet heaven greats, and it doesn’t need to.

Vampire Survivors veterans will have a sense of deja vu from the pixel art-styling and increasing enemy clusters. There’s some extra content and quality-of-life features bolted on here, but you’ll instantly know what you’re getting into.

When players start a run, they’re dropped into iconic locations from a top-down perspective in order to purge the area of ravenous xenos and chaos cultists. The onslaught of enemies grows increasingly fearsome as time wears on, with larger and more dangerous enemies joining the fray. As players dodge and defeat the alien threats, though, they provide experience points and items that exponentially ramp up player power.

Once you start getting your hands on an expanded arsenal of weaponry, it becomes obvious why Auroch Digital was the right choice for this project – it’s a development studio full of folks who obviously love the twin worlds of Warhammer, and that passion can be found in every nook and cranny of Warhammer Survivors.

The game’s visual style is striking, which is something I’ve come to expect from any Auroch Digital game – Warhammer Boltgun has richly detailed pixel art, and the development experience from those boomer shooters has translated extremely well to Warhammer Survivors’ 8-bit arcade trappings. The cost of entry is worth it just to see massive tyranid aliens and chaos space marines rendered in all their retro glory.

And the space marine power fantasy thrives here as players wield some of the most iconic space marine weapons, including gory chainswords, hard-hitting boltguns and face-melting flamers. What’s truly special, though, is how many of the game’s weapons and passive power-ups pay homage to the series’ tabletop roots – I was chuffed to see explosive D6 dice and mini figure glue, which both became a regular part of my screen-clearing builds.

One truly unique feature allows players to collect allies that wield weapons, instead of just building out a one-man arsenal. These allies trail behind the main character, which alters how players may approach hordes of enemies.

Certain characters unlock massive buffs if they continue adding allies to the party, which introduces another way to scale up damage very quickly. This doesn’t change how account-wide progression works, but it’s a new play style that shakes up the Vampire Survivors formula.

But it was when I discovered my favorite playable character in Warhammer Survivors that I started really noticing the game’s biggest weakness. I found myself enjoying the Sister of Battle’s gameplay, since she gets to wield a holy shield that repels enemies and damages evildoers who get too close with nearly constant pulses of light. As I continued to invest in this play style, I realized that this character was a nearly one-to-one re-creation of my Vampire Survivors main (Poe Ratcho, with his stinky demon-killing garlic).

It almost feels as though Auroch Digital was afraid to deviate too far from Poncle’s original vision for a bullet heaven game. The characters and weapons feel like reskins; the upgrade shop looks nearly identical, and even the in-game war chests that elite enemies drop have the same opening animation as the loot boxes from Vampire Survivors.

Warhammer Survivors is well-built, but often feels like a massive DLC for Vampire Survivors rather than a standalone game.

There’s plenty of meat on Warhammer Survivors’ bones. The Warhammer 40,000 and Age of Sigmar universes have their own progression tracks, with unique maps, characters and secrets to unlock. Survivors’ scale is remarkable – this game is probably twice as large as Vampire Survivors was when it launched from Early Access, and it could get even bigger with post-launch updates and future DLC.

If you love Warhammer and have never played a bullet heaven game before, Warhammer Survivors will likely ensnare you the same way Vampire Survivors did the rest of us in 2022. Figuring out effective weapon combinations, slaying thousands of oncoming foes and watching loot fly out of treasure chests with all the pomp and circumstance of a digital slot machine are all still surefire ways to flood your brain with dopamine.

But if you’ve delved deep into this genre and have enjoyed the immense mechanical advancements of later games, I suspect you’ll find Warhammer Survivors a bit lacking.

At its core, this is a game centered around achieving increasingly large damage numbers to defeat foes that continue to get faster and stronger until you’re overwhelmed – it’s a simple premise that can only be mastered through repetition. Yet Poncle’s award-winning formula started wearing thin for me this time around, and I say that as someone who believes the world is richer for having more action-packed Warhammer games and good Vampire Survivors clones in it.

Too many elements feel rehashed and reused (characters and weapon drops are the worst offenders), and Warhammer Survivors very quickly begins to feel like a carbon copy of a game I’d already played. Sure, it’s copying from an excellent game. But no difficulty spike or mystery is novel enough to remove my sense of fatigue, and I was left wishing there was some additional layer of progression or mechanical depth to keep me engaged between runs.

Warhammer Survivors currently commands an even higher price tag ($8) than its predecessor. Auroch Digital is making a big ask, especially since this game doesn’t benefit from Vampire Survivors’ multiple years of free content updates and DLC. Warhammer Survivors isn’t quite as expensive as its contemporary competitors, but it also lacks their innovations.

As it stands, I think this is a solid game – but as a pricey reskin, I wouldn’t recommend it over similar games like Vampire Hunters and Megabonk, unless you’re a Warhammer fan just looking for more ways to mow through enemies.

Warhammer Survivors is available now on PC, Nintendo Switch, Xbox Series X/S, PlayStation 5, iOS and Android for $8 and is included within Game Pass subscriptions.

With lower-cost campus designs driving expansion, Lincoln Educational Services is positioning its infrastructure for long-term growth.

#3091. Reddit’s New AI-Powered Reviews Are Already Controversial

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Tech > Services & Software > Online > Online Services

The platform's test of automated product review summaries is sparking concern that advertising will replace human advice.

Reddit announced on Tuesday that it’s testing Reviews, an AI-powered shopping feature that aggregates user comments into product summaries, commerce links, and pros-and-cons breakdowns. In a blog post, the company said it wants to organically use discussions on the platform, from conversations about skin care treatments or coffee to headphones, to help people “understand what a product is really like and feel confident deciding whether it’s right for them.”

The Reviews feature promises to make product research easier on a site that’s increasingly focused on shopping recommendations. But the announcement immediately rankled some Reddit users who are concerned it will degrade authentic human-to-human discussion and advice. Many Reddit moderators, or “mods,” tasked with keeping order of communities called subreddits, believe it’ll be hard to distinguish real opinions from straight-up advertising.

According to Reddit, the upcoming feature will surface product reviews in search results and through highlighted product mentions in comment threads, regardless of a group’s rules preventing the promotion of products by users or brands.

The test launch of Reviews, which was previewed in February and focused on electronics, will start with about 10,000 products across electronics, health and beauty, home and garden, and fashion and apparel. If the experiment works, Reddit plans to expand the feature outside the US and also increase the range of categories and products.

In a Reddit community for the moderators who enforce platform and subreddit rules, the new AI-powered shopping feature was greeted with skepticism and criticism. Writing in modnews, ProudnotLoud dubbed early tests “an ad-ridden, distracting mess” that made reading threads nearly impossible.

For moderators who work to keep commercial spam out of their subreddits, the feature poses an existential threat. User nerdshark warned that communities are already being actively targeted by stealth corporate campaigns, arguing that forcing Reviews into these spaces “does vulnerable communities a huge disservice,” especially without an opt-out mechanism.

Some Reddit admins have pushed back against the backlash, clarifying that the embedded product links are search shortcuts rather than paid placements. Yet users remain unconvinced. As CouncilofStrongs countered: “From a user experience, it is an ad.”

Reddit has also recently been testing advertising in search results, which could be a way for brands to reach Reddit users who click a product name even if they aren’t paying for placement in Reddit Reviews.

Given the amount of sites that focus heavily on human-centered reviews (you’re reading one of them), Reddit’s intent to aggregate product information through AI summaries could be seen as another way for traditional media publishers to have their content used without compensation.

But Reddit maintains the feature is purely informational. In a statement to CNET, a Reddit spokesperson said that Reviews relies exclusively on internal platform content and “does not source, scrape or republish third-party content.” The company said that because each review links to the original discussion, users on the platform “can explore the context and go deeper. “

Reddit also said that brands can’t buy ads to get into Reddit Reviews. “What appears in Reddit Reviews is shaped by Reddit communities, not paid placement,” the spokesperson said.

However, that reliance on organic Reddit activity brings its own vulnerabilities. One challenge Reddit may face with Reviews is trying to keep its AI focused on authentic human-written reviews versus posts that might come from marketers, coordinated astroturfing or AI-generated spam. Because the platform operates on anonymity, it’s facing an uphill battle with a massive influx of AI bots that could try to game content in Reviews.

The new feature comes alongside Reddit’s recent changes to the platform to detect spam or other manipulated content and keep bots out, including discontinuing support for RSS feeds and limiting access to its content API. The company is also restricting Old Reddit, a previous design version of the platform that has fewer ads.

A Reddit spokesperson told CNET that the platform has “the least amount of AI slop relative to other[s]” and that it is taking “numerous steps to prevent and enforce against inauthentic content.”

But while Reddit insists that Reviews will be centered on personal experience and uncorrupted by advertising dollars, many are worried the feature could blur the line between community research and automated e-commerce.

TL;DR: Mortgage rates went up today, but they're still in a much better place than this time last month.

Mortgage rates are higher today, but only by a little. And they're still hovering below 7%, which is much better than what we saw around this time last month.

The average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage ticked up to 6.98% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow. This is two basis points higher than Friday and five basis points higher than a week ago. (A basis point is one one-hundredth of a percentage point.)

Mortgage rates have more room to rise, as a stronger-than-expected jobs report reinforced expectations for a Federal Reserve rate hike in December.

Here are the average APRs we're seeing today, as well as movement over the past month for context:

As for what’s next: Tomorrow’s jobs report, showing October data, could potentially nudge mortgage rates in either direction. To understand the link between jobs data and mortgage rates, keep reading below the video.

» Take the next step: Compare mortgage rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders

Mortgage rates are constantly changing, since a major part of how rates are set depends on reactions to new inflation reports, job numbers, Fed meetings, global news ... you name it. For example, even tiny changes in the bond market can shift mortgage pricing.

This week, the Nerds are watching the October Consumer Price Index, which comes out on Tuesday. CPI is one of two key measures of inflation, which the Federal Reserve aims to keep in check relative to the strength of the labor market. (The Fed looks more closely at a different inflation measure, the Personal Consumption Expenditures Index, which comes out Nov. 25.)

Right now, the labor market is looking pretty darn strong: The October jobs report, released Friday from the Bureau of Labor Statistics, showed U.S. employers added 165,000 jobs in October, far more than economists expected, and unemployment edged down to 4.1%.

Raising the federal funds rate is the Fed’s main tool for bringing inflation down, but rate hikes are only on the table when the labor market is strong enough to handle it. Considering Friday’s jobs data, it’s looking fairly likely that the Fed will approve a rate hike when the committee meets Dec. 8-9. The Fed doesn't set mortgage rates directly, but an anticipated rate hike can put upward pressure on mortgage rates, which respond to investors’ expectations for the economy and Fed policy.

Still, a jump in mortgage rates isn’t a sure thing, and market sentiment could shift over the next month. October’s inflation data will capture the effect of the Fed’s last rate hike, which came in the middle of September. If that worked as intended and inflation shows signs of slowing, mortgage rates might remain around 7%.

Refinancing might make sense if today’s rates are at least 0.5 to 0.75 of a percentage point lower than your current rate (and if you plan to stay in your home long enough to break even on closing costs).

Also consider your goals: Are you trying to lower your monthly payment, shorten your loan term or turn home equity into cash? For example, you might be more comfortable with paying a higher rate for a cash-out refinance than you would for a rate-and-term refinance, so long as the overall costs are lower than if you kept your original mortgage and added a HELOC or home equity loan.

If the answer is yes, don’t get too hung up on whether you could be missing out on lower rates later; you can refinance down the road. Focus on getting preapproved, comparing lender offers, and understanding what monthly payment works for your budget.

NerdWallet’s affordability calculator can help you estimate your potential monthly payment. If a new home isn’t in the cards right now, there are still things you can do to strengthen your buyer profile. Take this time to pay down existing debts and build your down payment savings. Not only will this free up more cash flow for a future mortgage payment, it can also get you a better interest rate when you’re ready to buy.

Rate locks protect you from increases while your loan is processed, and with the market forever bouncing around, that peace of mind can be worth it.

#3087. Want Apple Intelligence for Your Home Security Camera? You’ll Need These 4 Things

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Apple Intelligence offers smart AI features for compatible cameras, but you’ll need to play by Apple’s rules. Here’s all the requirements.

Senior Editor / Home Security and Smart Home

Senior Editor / Home Security and Smart Home

In the past months Apple has unveiled a host of new Apple Intelligence and Siri AI features, with more on the way. And some features immediately caught my attention because they can enable security cameras on Apple devices in all-new ways. The most interesting option even adds video descriptions, essentially using AI to “read” your security clips and give you texts about what’s happening in them, so you don’t have to view them yourself.

It’s a nifty trick, one that I’ve seen come to Google Nest, Arlo, Ring, Blink and other home security camera companies in the past year or two. Now it’s Apple’s turn, but enabling this AI feature takes more work this time around. Apple wants to keep users inside its ecosystem, so there are more requirements than usual for smart video descriptions and similar capabilities. Let’s go through exactly what you’ll need.

Apple Intelligence doesn’t run on just any device. Your first requirement is an iPhone or iPad that can handle it. If you recently downloaded iOS 27 or iPadOS 27 and received an update about Apple Intelligence now being on your device, you should be good to go.

Specifically, you’ll need an iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max or iPhone 16 model or later to run these features. If you prefer using an iPad, you’ll need the iPad Mini (A17 Pro or later) or an iPad model with the M1 chip or later.

Before you start using security features with Apple Intelligence, make sure everything is updated – you’ll want the latest iOS if you don’t have it yet.

Smart home devices that work with Apple Home typically need a hub to pair with, and security cameras using Apple Intelligence are no exception. That means you’ll need another Apple device that can act as a hub, and you’ve got several choices.

Apple hubs include the second-gen HomePod, the HomePod Mini and Mini 2 or an Apple TV 4K model. Apple briefly gave some iPads the ability to become home hubs but then stopped, so an iPad won’t be sufficient here.

You’ll need a security camera that works well with Apple Home, but that’s easier said than done. If you can wait, Apple’s own security camera line, made in partnership with LG, should be here by the end of 2026, and should have the best results.

However, those Apple cams will be very expensive, so I understand if you want to look for a more affordable option. Not many security cams currently work with Apple, but one of the best brands is Aqara, like this Aqara G3650 camera hub ($140) I’m testing right now. Aqara models go down to $40, so there’s plenty of room to save here.

Note that, at least for the base subscription, I’ve seen reports that AI features like video descriptions only work with one camera at a time, so getting a whole fleet of cams won’t make much difference here. And speaking of subscriptions, there’s one final piece you’ll want.

Apple Intelligence features may require an advanced iCloud subscription.

You’ll want an iCloud Plus subscription to enable the full suite of Siri AI capabilities and avoid running into daily limits. But to be clear, even if you don’t use Siri AI, these security Apple Intelligence features will require at least a 2TB plan, which starts at $10 per month. That’s not surprising – video descriptions like this typically come with a subscription requirement, up to $20 per month in some cases.

Now you’ve got everything you need for Apple Intelligence security features. To get started, just go to Apple Home, go to Home Settings and make sure Apple Intelligence is toggled on. Then you should be able to choose an added camera to turn on video descriptions.

However, these factors do not influence our editors' opinions or ratings, which are based on independent research and analysis. Our partners cannot pay us to guarantee favorable reviews. Here is a list of our partners.

Chase's hotel and resort program, The Edit, gives some cardholders the chance to book stays at spectacular hotels.

Many premium credit cards have their own travel portals where you can earn and redeem your points. They also have a curated list of hotels with which they partner to offer elevated benefits to their cardholders who book directly through their program.

The Edit is Chase’s program, and similar to the Fine Hotels & Resorts program from American Express, travelers need to book a prepaid reservation directly through a Chase Travel channel and pay with their Chase card to receive the benefits.

What benefits do you receive when you book through the program? Well, they can be substantial.

At nearly 1,400 hotels and resorts, The Edit customers will enjoy:

If the hotel is an all-inclusive property, guests would instead receive a $200 property credit to use for experiences like spa treatments. While stays at hotels in The Edit Boutique Collection do include the other perks, those stays are not eligible for a room upgrade or early check-in/late checkout considerations.

The tradeoff of using The Edit program is that it does not necessarily always have the lowest rate. Sometimes you can find a lower rate directly with the hotel or another website. But, when you consider the list of benefits above, any differential in price can more than outweigh the extra cost.

While it belongs to Chase, The Edit is not open to all Chase cardholders. It is a dedicated perk for primary cardholders and authorized users of the Chase Sapphire Reserve® and J.P. Morgan Reserve cards, as well as primary Sapphire Reserve for Business℠ cardholders.

Even better is that these eligible Chase cards come with a total of $500 in credits that can be used at The Edit hotels each year. They are divided into two $250 credits that each must be used for at least a two-night stay. And when paying for the rest of your stay through The Edit, cardholders earn 8x Chase Ultimate Rewards® points per dollar spent. In addition, hotel stays booked through The Edit and labeled as “Loyalty Plus” are eligible to also earn points with any associated hotel loyalty program.

These are some of our favorite hotels in the program where you can take advantage of your annual $500 credits as well as earn significant Chase points for a prepaid stay.

This oasis in the desert enjoys distant views of the Atlas Mountains from its various pools and riad-like accommodation buildings. It also has a full-service spa, kids club and access to Al Maaden Golf course. Its Moroccan restaurant is worth a visit and offers cuisine from all of Morocco and the North African region (with many ingredients coming from the chef’s onsite garden). Guests can add a stash of World of Hyatt points to their account after a stay here, but be sure to look to see if it is “eligible” in the search results (as shown below).

Guests can arrive at this luxury resort by its own fleet of two sea planes that serve the three properties in the Four Seasons portfolio. (Two of the properties are in The Edit, the third is a private island: Four Seasons Maldives Kuda Huraa, Four Seasons Resort Maldives at Landaa Giraavaru and Four Seasons Maldives Private Island at Voavah, respectively.)

Overwater villas with their own pools and hammocks dangling over the sea, beach bungalows with private access pools and excellent dining (from Asian to Lebanese) are hallmarks of the resort. Its newest element is the AyurMa wellness program at the spa with onsite practitioners who guide guests on personalized, multiday journeys covering everything from nutrition to physical therapy.

This resort is designed around 64 pool suites and villas with access to a beautiful beachfront, swimming pools and a jungle spa. Its island location lies within the Gulf of Thailand near Koh Samui, and its beach is well-known for its famous Full Moon parties. Other activities, besides relaxing, include Muay Thai boxing, scuba diving, snorkeling, kayaking, stand-up paddle boarding and yoga sessions.

Anantara is part of Minor Hotels that are associated with the Discovery program, which means travelers can earn Discovery Dollars, even when booking via The Edit.

Along the Southbank Promenade, this luxury hotel has great views of the Melbourne skyline and is within walking distance of the city’s great shopping, museums and dining options. When you enter the lobby, the first thing you notice is the grand Waterford crystal chandelier, one of the largest in the Southern Hemisphere.

This is also one of the city’s biggest hotels, and it is highly regarded as a top hotel in town. Be sure to request one of the rooms with a balcony or terrace to take in the views.

Known by many as Dublin’s grande dame, this Autograph Collection member is fresh off the heels of a top-to-bottom renovation that renewed its interiors, but didn’t change its historic spirit. While renovation work will linger into 2027, the refreshed rooms are worth experiencing.

The hotel is where the drafting of the Irish Constitution took place, but today it serves as a hub for visiting elite and locals to mix and mingle. When booking through The Edit, members can earn Marriott Bonvoy points in addition to Chase Ultimate Rewards®.

This beachfront hotel is a favorite destination for European travelers who want a Dalmatian coastline view while also being in close proximity to the historic center of town. There are multiple pools, a beach club and spa for onsite entertainment. Radisson Rewards members would also be able to earn points for their stay.

Radisson is growing its portfolio of high-end hotels, resorts and luxury properties, which makes the loyalty program one not to overlook for Americans who may not be as familiar with it.

This city-center hotel is ideal for business travelers, but also attracts attention for its rooftop bar and restaurant. Chase cardholders using The Edit should think beyond just booking a vacation stay through the program because business trips can also yield significant Ultimate Rewards points bonuses. Just remember you need to book through The Edit with a prepaid, eligible rate.

In a historic bank building, the hotel’s Bauhaus-inspired design with colorful art make this more than just a standard business property. And like Kimpton properties worldwide, guests here can take advantage of morning coffee and refreshments in the lobby, an evening happy hour, free bikes and yoga mats to use, and of course the secret password. Mention that password (which changes seasonally) at reception to be eligible for a prize that could include drink vouchers or room upgrades among other things.

This family-friendly resort features the largest and first waterpark on the island (with three waterslides and a lazy river) as well as some of its finest dining venues, including the only high-end steakhouse on the island. Golfers can enjoy the island’s only 18-hole golf course here, too.

Because it's an independent resort, booking through The Edit is a great way to still earn points for your stay since it does not have a loyalty program of its own.

Celebrating 100 years, the hotel has unveiled renovations across the hotel, which sits in midtown Manhattan, and they will continue for the next year. Guests who book a Club rate or have the annual lounge benefit they can select as a Milestone Reward can visit the lobby-level club lounge here.

The building was built as part of the Grand Central Terminal design plan and now belongs to the Historic Hotels of America group. Guests who book through The Edit will receive IHG One Rewards for their stay and any eligible elite status perks.

The “Pink Palace of the Pacific” will celebrate its 100th anniversary in 2027 and is a famous hotel along one of Hawaii’s most famous beaches. This is one of many Marriott Bonvoy family hotels in Honolulu, and it is surrounded by lush gardens and has stunning ocean views. Guests can walk to nearby shopping, take the onsite history tour or snap photos with Diamond Head in the background. Guests can earn Marriott Bonvoy points for their stay, and elite status members can take advantage of any eligible perks.

This all-inclusive, family hotel is a great option for those looking for great dining, sunshine and oceanfront accommodations. Parents can enjoy the spa while kids are having fun in the kids club. Other activities include movie nights outside, painting classes, beach barbecues and lawn games. The resort is part of the Preferred Hotels & Resorts program, and earning Ultimate Rewards points for booking a stay through The Edit is a nice bonus.

Prepare for a new experience at one of the Chilean capital’s most posh hotels, and you can book your entire stay through The Edit. As a result, you would receive the perks of the program as well as Marriott Bonvoy points at the only Ritz-Carlton in South America.

Big changes at the hotel include new menus that refocus the restaurant cuisine on modern takes of Chilean recipes. The chef partners with a local farmer for produce, but goes one step further in being able to have first dibs on the best produce and herbs available each season. On the top floor, guests can enjoy a panoramic indoor swimming pool beneath a glass atrium, panoramic rooftop terrace and spa offering traditional Andean healing treatments.

Booking a hotel via The Edit leads to instant benefits like free breakfast, property credits, and early check-in and late checkout. While the rates may not always be the lowest you’ll find online, the perks that come with The Edit may more than outweigh any cost differential.

The Edit’s curated collection of hotels and resorts covers a broad range of high-end properties, and the program is only open to select Chase credit cardholders. When making a prepaid, eligible reservation through The Edit, the cardholder also receives 8x Ultimate Rewards points on top of the onsite perks that make this a great offer. Even better, if the property participates in its own loyalty program, Chase has worked out that members can double dip and earn Chase Ultimate Rewards® and the relevant hotel points and potential elite status perks, too (as long as it is labeled as “eligible” in the search function).

Don’t forget about the $500 in built-in credits that come with your card, which renew each year and only further the value with Chase’s The Edit program.

#3084. Top Wall Street analysts like these 3 dividend stocks for steady income

The stock market continues to grapple with volatility amid geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and concerns about the sustainability of the AI boom. Given this uncertainty, investors looking for steady income can add dividend-paying stocks to their portfolios.

Tracking the recommendations of top Wall Street analysts can help investors pick the right dividend stocks, as these experts assign their ratings after an in-depth analysis of a company's financials and ability to pay dividends consistently.

Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

Downstream energy company Phillips 66 (PSX) is this week's first dividend pick. With a quarterly dividend $1.27 per share (annualized dividend of $5.08), PSX offers a yield of 2.25%. The company recently reported solid Q2 earnings, as the Middle East conflict affected global supplies and drove up refining margins.

Following the Q2 print, TD Cowen analyst Jason Gabelman reiterated a buy rating on Phillips 66 and raised his price target to $255 from $240, reflecting higher 2026 earnings expectations and lower interest expense next year.

Gabelman highlighted the quarter-over-quarter reduction in Phillips 66's net debt, noting management's optimism at achieving its estimated $15.5 billion net debt target one year ahead of schedule. The 5-star analyst expects the company to end 2026 with a net debt of $14.6 billion.

"The [balance sheet] improvement could re-establish PSX as a go-to defensive refiner," said Gabelman.

Management agreed that PSX's payout ratio lagged year-to-date, but expects buybacks to increase in the second half. Gabelman said Phillps indicated the possibility of a larger dividend hike following an annual increase of 5% over the past two years.

Gabelman ranks No. 554 among more than 12,400 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 66% of the time, delivering an average return of 14.9%. See Phillips 66 Statistics on TipRanks.

Crescent Energy (CRGY) is an exploration and production company with activities focused in the Eagle Ford, Permian and Uinta Basins. Earlier this month, the company reported better-than-expected Q2 earnings and announced a quarterly dividend of $0.12 per share, payable on August 31. At an annualized dividend of $0.48 per share, CRGY boasts a dividend yield of about 4%.

In reaction to Q2 results, Evercore analyst Stephen Richardson reaffirmed a buy rating on Crescent Energy stock with a price target of $18. He noted continued strength in the company's performance, with second-quarter oil production and cash flow surpassing the Street's expectations.

"CRGY's cash flow exceeded expectations by 10%, reinforcing its trajectory of capital efficiency," said Richardson.

The 5-star analyst highlighted that Crescent raised its full-year oil production guidance, citing the effective integration of the Vital Energy acquisition. Specifically, Crescent tripled its synergy target from the Vital Energy deal to as much as $300 million, significantly reducing the effective purchase price. This reflects Crescent's solid execution following the acquisition, Richardson said.

Additionally, the analyst noted that Crescent's capital spending is and heading toward the lower end of management's prior guidance, indicating disciplined financial controls.

Richardson ranks No. 579 among more than 12,400 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 65% of the time, delivering an average return of 12.5%. See Crescent Energy Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

Finally, Viper Energy (VNOM) is effectively controlled by Diamondback Energy. Viper owns and acquires mineral and royalty interests in oil-weighted basins, mainly the Permian in West Texas. Viper recently announced its Q2 2026 results and declared a 32% hike in its base dividend, effective in the third quarter of 2026. The new base dividend indicates a 4.5% annualized yield.

Viper also removed its quarterly commitment to return at least 75% of cash available for distribution. The company believes that this move will ensure increased flexibility to make opportunistic share repurchases and pursue accretive mergers and acquisitions.

Following the Q2 results, TD Cowen analyst Aaron Bilkoski reiterated a buy rating on Viper, slightly raising his price target to $59 from $58. Bilkoski said Viper's solid Q2 performance supports his view that the strength in oil prices and rising operator activity are driving higher production.

"Viper has delivered, and we forecast will continue to deliver, one of the highest production per share growth profiles in our royalty universe" through the end of 2027, said Bilkoski. He believes Viper deserves a premium valuation, given its above-average growth.

The 5-star analyst said that while the biggest surprise in the quarter was Viper's revision to its shareholder return framework, he doesn't believe that the move indicates a significant change to its underlying strategy. Under the new framework, a larger portion of excess free cash flow is expected to be allocated to share repurchases than to variable dividends, Bilkoski said.

Bilkoski ranks No. 719 among more than 12,400 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 57% of the time, delivering an average return of 12%. See Viper Energy Financials on TipRanks.

#3082. Prediction: Here's What the Nasdaq Will Do in the Last 2 Months of 2026

The Nasdaq recently fell into correction territory.

The Nasdaq Composite has had ups and downs this year, but in recent times, the downs have won out. The tech-heavy benchmark fell into correction territory. Why has the index slipped? A variety of elements have represented headwinds this year. Investors have worried about rising inflation and the potential interest rate increases put into place to contain it.

And the biggest concern of all might be regarding the future of artificial intelligence (AI). Investors question whether big tech's spending on new data centers and equipment will be worth the effort -- or if the revenue opportunity will fall short. All of this has put pressure on tech stocks and, therefore, the Nasdaq, in 2026.

On top of this, Democrats, who have been cautious regarding AI, scored majorities in both the House of Representatives and the Senate in the U.S. midterm elections last week. This reinforced investors' concerns about regulation and limitations on data center growth.

Against this backdrop, you might be wondering what the Nasdaq will do in the last two months of 2026. Here's my prediction.

First, let's take a look at the Nasdaq and tech story so far. As mentioned, technology companies are heavily weighted in the benchmark, so if they are having a good or bad day, the Nasdaq will reflect that. Apple, Nvidia, and Microsoft lead the Nasdaq-100, the index of the largest non-financial companies traded on Nasdaq, with weightings of more than 10% each.

Over the past three years, as the AI boom progressed, the Nasdaq Composite advanced, gaining more than 100% until the recent dip. This is as AI companies reported strong revenue growth and investors got excited about the current and future earnings opportunities. AI was seen as the next big thing in technology, and investors wanted to bet on it early to maximize their gains.

Stocks climbed so much, however, that valuations started to look lofty. And investors began to worry about the return on investment for tech giants paying for the AI infrastructure build-out. Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft, and Meta Platforms pledged to spend more than $700 billion this year alone. This, along with higher inflation and a tightening of the credit market, has periodically weighed on the performance of tech stocks. And just recently, the Democrats' victory stirred up concern about a potential slowdown in AI growth.

Now, here's my prediction for the last two months of the year. While this month may be a difficult one for the Nasdaq, I predict that the index will advance in December and post a double-digit gain for the year. We aren't far from such a gain now, with the increase being more than 8% from the start of the year through Nov. 9.

History shows that the index has climbed four times in the November-December period over the past six years, and the end of the year is generally known as being a strong period for stocks. The S&P 500 often benefits from a "Santa Claus" rally, with the index finishing positive almost 80% of the time during that period, according to Britannica Money. (That period is the last five trading days of December and the first two days of January.)

So, history supports my prediction, but I'm not basing my ideas on that alone. I also think the Nasdaq may climb because the long-term AI growth story hasn't changed. Even if it faces certain headwinds or a slowdown, quality, well-established tech companies are likely to generate significant growth from their AI investments and products over the long run.

Meanwhile, some of these companies are trading at interesting valuations right now due to the recent decline. Investors are likely to recognize this and may decide to add some of these players to their portfolios at the end of the year -- to prepare for a potential rebound next year.

And that could help the Nasdaq, after falling into correction territory, advance in the last weeks of the year.

VA mortgage borrowers are quietly navigating a knowledge gap. Here’s how to close it.

If your understanding of a VA home loan starts and ends with “it’s for the military,” you’re not alone. For many eligible veterans and service members, the intricate workings (and benefits) of this U.S. government-backed mortgage are obscured behind lackluster guidance.

While there are classes and resources available, the military is broadly wary of steering members in a specific direction, says Alex Rodino, a real estate agent and U.S. Army veteran who served 10 years as an infantry officer and military advisor. “A lot of the course material is just very generic,” he says.

And that’s not a surprise. Considering the sheer size and scope of the military, providing personalized advice on VA loans to all its members would be no easy task.

That leaves real estate agents and lenders as the last line of defense, which is where a big part of the knowledge gap exists. Rodino purchased his first home in 2020 with a VA loan and says he didn’t like how ignorant he felt during the process.

“The reason I actually got my real estate license to begin with was because of that experience I had,” Rodino says. “Looking back on it, I had a lot of questions that didn't really get answered.”

But how can VA borrowers navigate this knowledge gap without having to become mortgage experts in their spare time? Here are some of the most important things to know when considering a VA loan, according to the financial experts and borrowers who have lived it.

“My mortgage broker said, hey, you might qualify for this, look it up,” says Elizabeth Valente, a real estate investor and former U.S. Army officer who bought her first home using a VA loan in 2021. When it came to the application process, she felt crucial information wasn’t readily available to her or fully explained.

In hindsight, Valente says, working with an agent or lender who had detailed VA loan experience would have been beneficial. Not only would it help untangle the specific paperwork and appraisal requirements, but that expertise offers an important layer of support for military borrowers.

“For some processes in the military, it's very hand-holding,” Valente says. “I'll tell you what to wear, what to bring, when to be there.” But that’s not always true when transitioning back to civilian life, and parsing specifics of a loan process can be challenging. “I don't think a typical Realtor would understand what that person's going through,” Valente says.

Finding professionals with the right expertise involves asking questions — and lots of them.

“If I'm the smartest person in the room, we have an issue,” Valente says. “Don't be afraid to tell someone if something doesn't make sense or if you don't understand the numbers.”

Before agreeing to work with a lender or mortgage broker, ask how their process works, what companies they work with, and how familiar they are with VA loans. Treat the initial conversation like an interview — you’re hiring them, not the other way around.

Knowing where to find your Certificate of Eligibility (COE) and how much you might be eligible to borrow is the responsibility of the person applying, Valente says. “All that information — it is available in the [VA] website but you really have to dig for it.”

And this information isn’t recreational reading — your COE lists your "basic entitlement," which is a crucial figure in VA lending. If you have full basic entitlement, the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) generally guarantees 25% of the loan, which in most cases lets you put 0% down.

Why? With a quarter of the loan guaranteed by the VA, the lender is more protected and thus more willing to forgo a down payment.

So how do you know if you have full basic entitlement? Look for the figure $36,000 on your COE. This dollar amount represents full entitlement. Technically, basic entitlement is for loans up to $144,000, but then your bonus entitlement kicks in and you can go higher. The VA doesn’t set loan limits when you have full entitlement — though your lender will still decide how much you can borrow based on your income, debts, credit and the home’s appraised value.

Let’s say you want to buy a home in Fayetteville, North Carolina, and you need a $200,000 loan. In order to put no money down, your entitlement needs to cover at least 25% of the loan amount — in this example, that’s $50,000. After you purchase the home, your COE will show your basic entitlement as $0 and the entitlement charged to a previous loan as $50,000.

“Serving in the military is a unique investing opportunity that most people don't get,” Rodino says. “I wish someone had told me to buy a house when I got to my first duty station.”

If he’d known it was possible or understood how, Rodino says he would have been able to buy in 2017, move in 2020, rent out his first home and then repeat the process. “I'd have three by now and the first one would probably be paid off.”

This particular plan is partly based on the unique schedule of many military members. “Generally, you're moving anywhere from two to four to six years,” Rodino says. Owning multiple properties also leverages two big (and often misunderstood) perks of the VA loan: It’s possible to have more than one active loan at the same time, and after one year, you may be able to convert your primary residence to a rental.

Let’s go back to Fayetteville, North Carolina. After two years, you decide to rent out the home because you’re moving to Bell County, Texas. The home you want to buy in Bell County is $300,000, and in order to make no down payment, you need the VA to guarantee 25% of the loan ($75,000).

Because you no longer have full basic entitlement — remember, you already have an active VA loan elsewhere — your entitlement is capped at 25% of the conforming loan limit in the county where you plan to buy, minus what’s already being used on your first loan ($50,000 in our Fayetteville example).

Now for the math: The current conforming loan limit in Bell County is $832,750. Multiply this figure by 25% and subtract the $50,000 already in use: You have $158,187.50 of entitlement available to you — plenty to guarantee the $75,000 needed on the new loan.

If all of this sounds overwhelming, you’re not wrong. There are resources out there to help you figure all of this out, Rodino says. “The problem is, they're not always practical or they're not always apparent.”

The VA has a website that can walk you through entitlement calculations, but you should also ask your lender, broker or agent. If you’re working with experienced folks, they’ll be able to explain these details and help you get the most out of the VA’s guarantees.

The key takeaway is this: While each VA loan must initially be for a primary residence, borrowers can leverage their entitlement to build an investment portfolio without needing to cough up large down payments.

But these examples don’t consider all of the factors that go into approvals. Like most mortgages, your income, debts and assets dictate your eligibility. And although the VA doesn’t impose credit score minimums, most lenders do — NerdWallet's analysis shows 620 is a common floor.

It’s also important to note that a VA loan’s 0% down isn’t free. VA loans carry a funding fee based on how much you’re putting down and whether it’s your first or subsequent use (certain disabled veterans are exempt). You can pay this up front at closing or roll it into the loan amount; again, your team of professionals should be able to walk you through your options.

“I think there's the assumption that this is what we do: We get our VA home loan and we go buy a home,” says Julie Soares, financial readiness director for the Wounded Warrior Project. When we’re given access to a benefit that offers discounts and perks, it can be hard not to take advantage of it. But this is why financial awareness is critical.

There are a lot of conversations happening right now around homeownership and whether it’s the right choice, especially as affordability remains challenging. So if you haven’t heard it recently, here’s a reminder: Buying property is not the only way to build wealth or create financial security.

“The financial readiness program at Wounded Warrior Project is really leaning into getting further upstream in those conversations,” Soares says. Having a clear understanding of your benefits before you need to use them allows you to make more informed choices.

While it's helpful to understand your entitlement and what you may be eligible to borrow, you don't have to know every little detail about mortgages, or navigate the process alone. Sometimes, the most important thing to know about VA loans is where to turn for help.

If you are unsure of your eligibility or want more information about home loans, you can call the VA's home loans hotline at 877-827-3702.

“Please reach out to Wounded Warrior Project, reach out to the VA, reach out to any service organization,” Soares says. “Not one organization is gonna be able to fix or solve all of these problems. We have to do this as a group.”

#3079. Is KKR a Buy After Its Latest Earnings Report?

The financial company posted an impressive jump in adjusted earnings.

One of the most seasoned and distinctive financial companies on the scene, KKR (KKR +2.81%) won some positive attention from investors early in the week. That's because the company started it off by publishing a quarterly earnings report that easily beat analyst estimates. KKR has always been a prominent company in its niche, and in the wake of earnings, it was a popular one. That doesn't necessarily mean it's a buy, however, so let's try to evaluate its performance on that basis.

While KKR topped consensus estimates -- more on that in a moment -- it actually saw a year-over-year decline in total revenue under generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) during the third quarter. This fell to $4.56 billion from $5.53 billion in the same frame of 2025. The drop was due to a slide in the business that comprises much of the company's take, insurance; this declined to slightly over $2.8 billion from the year-ago tally of $3.78 billion. KKR's total assets under management (AUM), meanwhile, rose by 11% to $804 billion.

The other arm of the company's operations, asset management and strategic holdings, rose during the period. The increase was modest, however, with only incremental growth to $1.76 billion.

Non-GAAP (adjusted) net income rose despite the revenue slide. It improved by a very sturdy 29% to $1.6 billion, or $1.78 per share. Much of this derived from a 27% jump in fee-related earnings to $1.3 billion.

With the caveat that the financials of asset managers and (to a lesser extent) insurers can be tricky to estimate, KKR's fundamentals were well above the pundit consensus numbers. On average, analysts tracking the company's stock were modeling only $2.69 billion for revenue, and $1.59 per share for adjusted net profit.

Essentially, KKR is a business anchored by steady revenue earners, namely the insurance operations and the fees and related revenue derived from its considerable asset management activities. The company balances this with its far more up-and-down investment activity, as it directly invests in a variety of assets to exit them at a profit for itself and its limited partners. When these exits are successful, the revenue generated can be substantial.

KKR has also been deeply involved in the capital markets for decades, and because it operates in both equity and debt verticals, there's a built-in hedge in this business.

The company is a financial sector powerhouse, and despite the ultimately up-and-down nature of its business, it usually manages to net a relatively high-margin profit. But all in all, it thrives when markets and companies thrive, and the economy may be heading into more challenging times. Since inflation persists, there's scope for fresh Federal Reserve interest rate hikes. Higher rates make the financing that powers KKR's deals more expensive and less available (therefore not as lucrative in the aggregate).

To me, all this means that KKR is a sharp operator, but one whose business model has a higher-than-average level of inherent volatility. I'd flag it as a buy only for investors with a long-term horizon who don't mind an occasionally bumpy ride along the way.

#3078. GE Vernova's Orders Jumped 96%. The Number Hiding Underneath Is Electrification's 9% Decline.

GE Vernova's third-quarter 2026 results were strong, but is the 9% decline in electrification orders a problem hiding in plain sight?

GE Vernova's (GEV -3.90%) third-quarter 2026 sales rose 27%, and its earnings rose 193% year over year. It is hard to complain about that performance, but the quarter wasn't all good news. For example, while orders rose 96% across the company, its electrification division saw orders fall by 9%. Don't get too worked up about it; there's a reason, and, in the end, it probably isn't a big deal. Here's why.

GE Vernova makes the turbines that generate electricity. The build-out of AI data centers currently taking place has dramatically increased electricity demand. And, in turn, that has increased the demand for the turbines that GE Vernova makes. At this point, the company's backlog is up to a massive $197 billion. That suggests this industrial giant has plenty of room for growth ahead, even if new order growth slows down.

A slowdown may be on some investors' minds as they look at the 9% drop in orders in the company's electrification division. But some perspective is needed to properly assess that figure. For starters, the big story right now is power, where GE Vernova generated $21.8 billion in orders. Electrification's $5.4 billion and wind's $2.1 billion are less meaningful to the overall story. And while electrification's $5.4 billion was down compared to the prior year, the division is still generating new orders.

But there's still more to the story. The year-over-year drop in orders is due to the third quarter of 2025 benefiting from unusually large orders. In fact, in the third quarter of 2026, the book-to-bill ratio was 1.4x for this division. That means it added more orders than it could fill, which is a sign of strength on the orders front. So, when you look more closely, electrification's 9% decline in orders doesn't seem like a particularly big deal for GE Vernova.

There is a lot going on in the world right now, from the political to the technological. Investors are worried about the future, and any bit of bad news could feel extra troubling. GE Vernova's third quarter was good, with a slight negative hiding underneath it. Don't overreact to the negative. Indeed, few quarters are 100% positive, and the negative was there for a good reason (an unusually strong third quarter for electrification in 2025) and is unlikely to be a lingering or material problem over the long term (highlighted by the division's 1.4x book-to-bill ratio).

The airline’s newest lounge will be the second-largest in the network, offering flyers an upgraded experience at Dulles.

You’ll no longer have to go to the basement to get into a United Club at Washington Dulles International Airport.

The brand-new United Club in the new IAD Concourse E spans nearly 40,000 square feet across an upstairs floor and can seat 630 passengers, making it a significant upgrade to the carrier’s existing lounge portfolio at the airport. It’s the second-largest United Club after its newest lounge in Houston, which opened just weeks earlier.

The new lounge by gates E14 and E16 opens to customers Nov. 10, 2026. United invited me to a media preview of the lounge, and here’s what you can expect inside.

The lounge features several nods to D.C.’s iconic landmarks and monuments, as well as the region’s natural beauty.

When you first enter the lounge, you’ll need to scan your boarding pass and then head up the escalators (stairs and elevators are also available) to get to the lounge.

One of my favorite design features as a former D.C. resident is that escalator ride up, which has been recreated to feel like you’re inside a Metro station.

Thankfully, the escalator ride is not as long as at some stations. Looking at you, Dupont Circle!

Once you're upstairs, you’ll walk into the heart of the lounge, with two buffet stations, a centerpiece bar and plenty of seating options, whether you’re traveling as a group or by yourself. (More on food and beverage options later.)

It’s impossible to miss the soaring ceilings in this lounge, especially compared to the bunker-like atmosphere at some of the existing United Clubs.

Don’t forget to look up, where you’ll see a cherry blossom sculpture, an homage to one of the region’s most popular attractions.

There are also two additional lounging areas on both sides of the central area. One is inspired by the Blue Ridge Mountains, which you can see in the distance.

The other has a cherry blossom theme, with light fixtures that branch out from the ceiling.

Massive windows run throughout the lounge, allowing in tons of natural light and offering fantastic views of the airfield. United has a major presence at IAD, so expect to see plenty of United planes.

The United Club has a full kitchen, allowing it to offer upgraded food options compared to its existing lounges at IAD.

You can expect to find sandwiches, salads and hot protein dishes. The lounge also had a ramen bar and a chili bar set up during my visit.

The two buffet stations are located right next to each other, with a dessert station in between.

If you want something to drink, you can head to the bar or one of the hydration stations throughout the space.

There’s plenty of seating at the bar, which has a double archway design. There are also large TVs if you’re trying to keep up with one of Washington’s many sports teams.

The United Club has eight phone booths for those who need to make a call. They’re split between the two lounging areas in the club.

You'll also find a single-stall private restroom, a wellness room, and dedicated men’s and women’s restrooms.

There are no showers in this lounge. To access a shower in a United lounge, you’ll need to head to the Polaris Lounge, reserved exclusively for eligible business class passengers flying on United and select partner airlines.

You can access the United Club by holding elite status, a lounge membership, the right credit card or an eligible premium cabin ticket.

If there’s availability, United sells day passes at the door for flights departing within three hours. You’ll also need a valid same-day boarding pass on a United or Star Alliance flight.

Holding the right credit card is probably the easiest way to get in. United’s most high-end card comes with a United Club membership, while others might offer one-time passes.

If you’re looking for a United lounge, the newest club in Concourse E is where you want to be. It offers more space, lots of light and elevated food options compared to other United Clubs.

Its massive footprint could also ease overcrowding, a common complaint with other lounges.

One thing to consider is location. The concourses at IAD are spread out, and you may need to take a mobile lounge or train to get there. If you want to check out the lounge, make sure you give yourself enough time to get to your gate.

#3076. Swarmer: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors

Swarmer's shift to selling complete defense systems directly to governments rests on combat-tested technology already used in Ukraine.

On its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Nov. 10, 2026, Swarmer (SWMR -2.23%) announced a pivot from selling business-to-business (B2B) software to corporate drone makers to manufacturing end-to-end defense hardware directly for government buyers. Controlling both physical hardware and autonomous software enables the business to capture higher contract values across ground vehicles, quadcopters, and air defense systems. Three things management said stand out.

Owning both physical defense hardware and autonomous software lets the company sell complete combat kits directly to government agencies. This reduces reliance on third-party drone manufacturers to bring its technology to market.

Acquiring Ratel Robotics brings unmanned ground vehicles (UGVs), which are land-based robotic combat vehicles, and an existing $86 million government contract backlog into the business. Ratel generated $32.5 million in revenue during the third quarter of 2026 alone.

A memorandum of understanding (MOU), which is a preliminary commercial agreement, with Vectus Air Defense outlines substantial purchase intent for complete air defense systems. Each system carries an estimated manufacturer's suggested retail price (MSRP) between $5 million and $6 million.

Manufacturing capacity is expanding each quarter to fulfill heavy government demand, positioning the company to transition from small-scale software support toward large-scale hardware delivery.

Field-tested technology, integrated hardware-software architecture, and direct government relationships provide structural defense advantages as leadership monitors production expansion and contract fulfillment.

#3074. Ray Dalio says Bessent move is sign that a debt crisis is getting closer; recommends gold and bitcoin

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's debt buyback announcement this week fits into a broader pattern that can signal a forthcoming crisis, according to billionaire investor Ray Dalio.

The Bridgewater Associates founder said Bessent's plan to increase government debt purchases may portend trouble for the U.S. economy. Coupled with the Japanese government reducing its U.S. bond market exposure and surging long-dated American bond yields, Dalio said investors may want to prepare their portfolios for increased risk by owning cryptocurrencies and gold.

"I am confident that the government's financial condition is at an inflection point," Dalio wrote in a LinkedIn post published Friday. "If this is not dealt with now, the debts will build up to levels where they can't be managed without great trauma."

Dalio noted that the Treasury Department has "only limited capacity" to buy back bonds. Bessent told CNBC on Thursday that his team was going to "make a market" and that the purchases would likely top $4 billion.

The U.S. is spending about 40% more than it's bringing in, resulting in the burgeoning budget deficit, Dalio said. The U.S. budget deficit topped $432 billion in July, but Bessent told CNBC that it's likely peaked under President Donald Trump's administration.

Bessent said in the interview that a team was looking at ways to shrink spending by hundreds of billions of dollars. But Dalio said there is "very little ability" to do so given that it is either committed or considered essential.

After years of overspending, Dalio said total debt now dwarfs what the U.S. brings in each year. If the U.S. government was a business, Dalio said debt service payments would come in at roughly $11 trillion — about 200% of annual revenue.

Dalio, 77, warned the cost of repaying principal and servicing the debt will only grow over time.

To solve this, Dalio said the U.S. needs to carefully employ a three-part strategy to get the budget deficit down to 3% of gross domestic product.

First, Dalio said the U.S. government needs to reduce its spending. Second, he said tax revenue needs to be raised. Finally, the New York native and Harvard Business School alumni said lower interest rates were needed.

"All three need to happen concurrently so as to prevent any one from being too large," Dalio said. "If any one is too large, the adjustment will be traumatic."

Dalio cautioned against ramming through these adjustments by "force." For instance, "it would be very bad if the Federal Reserve unnaturally forced interest rates down," he said.

Dalio said it's important to to take steps now, while the economy is healthy. An economy in recession requires increased government spending, he said.

Dalio said the exact timing of a debt crisis can be swayed by variables ranging from military conflict to political change. On its current trajectory, the U.S. could enter such a crisis in as early as one year or as late as five. "My guess, which I suppose will be a bad one, is that it will come in three years, give or take two, if the course we're on is not changed."

To prepare, Dalio recommended investors are underweight debt assets, such as bonds.

As much as 10% to 15% of a portfolio could land in gold, as well as "a bit" of bitcoin, the hedge fund founder said.

Dalio's post came at the tail end of a volatile week for U.S. financial markets. Rising long-term Treasury yields have pressured stocks, leading the S&P 500 to snap a a three-week-long advance.

#3073. Prediction Markets Are Arriving in Your Investing App, and That Makes Us Nervous

Its articles, interactive tools and other content are provided to you for free, as self-help tools and for informational purposes only. They are not intended to provide investment advice. NerdWallet does not and cannot guarantee the accuracy or applicability of any information in regard to your individual circumstances. Examples are hypothetical, and we encourage you to seek personalized advice from qualified professionals regarding specific investment issues. Our estimates are based on past market performance, and past performance is not a guarantee of future performance.

We believe everyone should be able to make financial decisions with confidence. And while our site doesn’t feature every company or financial product available on the market, we’re proud that the guidance we offer, the information we provide and the tools we create are objective, independent, straightforward — and free.

So how do we make money? Our partners compensate us. This may influence which products we review and write about (and where those products appear on the site), but it in no way affects our recommendations or advice, which are grounded in thousands of hours of research. Our partners cannot pay us to guarantee favorable reviews of their products or services. Here is a list of our partners.

Prediction markets are booming, but that doesn’t make them a sound investment strategy.

The investing information provided on this page is for educational purposes only. NerdWallet, Inc. does not offer advisory or brokerage services, nor does it recommend or advise investors to buy or sell particular stocks, securities or other investments.

Around this time every year, we conduct NerdWallet’s annual broker review process. We assess what’s changed in the industry, discuss which brokerage features matter most (and which ones now matter less), and finally, we do the work by opening accounts to test them.

Prediction markets, which have made their way into some of the most popular investing apps, came up more than we expected in testing this year.

At first, we decided to simply collect information on who does and doesn’t offer access to them, without intending to reward or penalize a broker either way. It would be a neutral presentation of facts, not something that would factor into how we scored a broker.

But one afternoon, all together in the office, we confronted an uncomfortable question: “Do prediction markets, and such easy access to them within an investment app, go against NerdWallet’s editorial house views?”

After careful consideration, we all agreed: they do.

So we started to configure our 2027 rubric with a firmer stance against this trendy feature, penalizing brokers that actively market sports and entertainment event contracts, and whose prediction markets come with few, if any, guardrails.

We’ve distilled our discussion down to three main points:

These products are being marketed alongside investments.

We fear they could be discouraging long-term investing.

Let’s start here: Many aspects of trading could be seen as gambling-adjacent. Options, futures, highly leveraged single-day equity bets and even crypto can all easily fall into the “highly speculative” category. So why are we picking on prediction markets in particular?

In our view, a key differentiator is a much lower barrier to entry with few in-app guardrails in place.

Most of the products we mentioned above require some level of fluency — and at times even permission from the broker — to dabble in. To trade options, for example, you need to answer questions about your investing proficiency, your finances and more. And even after approval, the terminology required to trade can be so intimidating that the language itself can become an indirect deterrent.

Event contracts, which form the backbone of prediction markets, are largely presented in the vernacular, and our testing showed approval to trade them is completed with a few taps from the home screen. Moreover, their content is often unrelated to finance — according to a May 2026 report by the Pew Research Center, around 80% of volume on the prediction market platform Kalshi was for sports events[1]Pew Research Center. Trading Volume on Prediction Markets Has Soared in Recent Months. Accessed Nov 2, 2026. View all sources .

Answering a binary question (yes/no; this/that), posed in everyday language about a familiar topic — something like, “Will the Knicks beat the Spurs on Sunday?” — can be far less daunting than figuring out what an options chain is or understanding forex pairs.

In other words, what makes prediction markets accessible to a wider audience is also what makes them problematic, especially when housed within an investing account. Which brings us to our next point.

On the platforms that feature them, we found that prediction markets almost always appear alongside stock and ETF trading. We think this is a mistake. What has made these mobile-first investing apps so good for so long (making it easy to move, manage and invest money through a beautiful interface) is what’s now making us nervous.

For example, most investing platforms let users do any number of smart things with idle cash. They could open an Individual Retirement Account (IRA), a custodial account or a robo-managed portfolio all through a single app. But now, they can dip into that same pot of money to bet on whether Beyoncé or Alicia Keys will play the Super Bowl halftime show.

But is anyone actually trading these event contracts? Let’s use data from publicly traded brokers that offer prediction markets to explore this.

In Q3 2026, Robinhood’s revenue from event contracts rose more than 600% year over year to $173 million, while the number of event contracts traded grew more than sevenfold to 16.4 billion[2]Robinhood. Robinhood Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results. Accessed Nov 2, 2026. View all sources . This was the second-highest source of transaction revenue behind options trading. In a forecast reported on by Cointelegraph, Bernstein analysts projected Robinhood’s prediction markets could drive $1.7 billion in annual revenue by 2028[3]Yahoo Finance. Bernstein Sees Robinhood Prediction Markets Reaching $1.7 Billion in Revenue by 2028, Topping Crypto. Accessed Nov 2, 2026. View all sources .

Coinbase's Q1 2026 quarterly report called prediction markets “one of its fastest-scaling products ever, driven by strong retail interest[4]Coinbase. Coinbase Q1 Financial Results Show Resilient Financial Performance Driven by New All-Time High Crypto Trading Volume Market Share. Accessed Nov 2, 2026. View all sources ."

In a call discussing Webull’s Q2 results, U.S. CEO Anthony Denier noted trading volume in Webull’s nascent prediction market product grew about 70% quarter over quarter[5]Gloom. Webull (BULL) Q2 2026 earnings call transcript. Accessed Nov 3, 2026. View all sources .

Gemini’s Q2 report shows prediction market volume rose 93% quarter over quarter[6]Gemini. Shareholder Update Q2 2026. Accessed Nov 2, 2026. View all sources .

So, now that we’ve established that these markets are growing in popularity — and investing platforms appear to have a large incentive to lean into them — how are all those event contract traders faring? That brings us to our final point.

Is all this even worth it? Several studies show how hard it is to actually turn a profit in prediction markets. Here are a few:

One study, conducted by researchers at ESSEC Business School, HEC Montréal and the University of Toronto's Rotman School of Management, covered 2.4 million Polymarket accounts across $67 billion in trading volume between November 2022 and March 2026, and found that 69% of users lost money[7]SSRN. Who Wins and Who Loses In Prediction Markets? Evidence from Polymarket. Accessed Nov 2, 2026. View all sources . Moreover, the top 1% of users who made a profit accounted for about 76% of all gains. Translation: Even if you did turn a profit, there’s a good chance you didn’t make much.

A Bloomberg analysis supports this: From January 2025 to April 2026, more than 100,000 Polymarket accounts lost at least $1,000[8]Bloomberg. Most Prediction Market Traders Are Losing Money While Bots Rack Up Gains. Accessed Nov 3, 2026. View all sources . Of the 2 million active wallets studied, almost half made or lost less than $10 during the period, while far fewer accounts collected larger profits.

A separate Wall Street Journal analysis echoed the same trend: 67% of Polymarket profits go to 0.1% of accounts, and more than 70% of Polymarket users lost money[9]The Wall Street Journal. Why Almost Everyone Loses—Except a Few Sharks—on Prediction Markets. Accessed Nov 3, 2026. View all sources .

While there is far less data available on Kalshi trades (Polymarket runs on a public blockchain, making it easy to extract and analyze data), a Kalshi spokesperson confirmed in the Wall Street Journal analysis above that one month of data in 2026 showed there were 2.9 unprofitable users to each profitable user[10]Wall Street Journal. Why Almost Everyone Loses—Except a Few Sharks—on Prediction Markets. Accessed Nov 10, 2026. View all sources .

The first study above discusses how event contract trading is binary and zero-sum: If one trader wins, another loses. This means traders allocating money to these instruments could be missing out on aspects of equity markets that have helped create long-term wealth for previous generations.

“Unlike equity markets, there is no equity premium, no dividends, and no passive investment options. Their short maturities naturally encourage short-horizon trading, which is precisely what the behavioral finance literature has suggested is most destructive to wealth accumulation. Given the rapid growth of these platforms and their role as a potential entry point for young investors, understanding who bears the losses has direct implications for investor welfare and market regulation.”

As a reminder, the vast majority of Polymarket users bore the losses.

At NerdWallet, our mission has always been to help people make smarter financial decisions, so we’re sticking by that. Starting with our 2027 ratings, brokers that offer easy access to sports and entertainment event contracts will lose points in our scoring system because we believe this new product has the potential to harm long-term wealth building and doesn’t belong in investing platforms.

So, what’s a better way forward? Bring back the friction and make prediction markets a separate app. Financial institutions, businesses and individuals can still explore legitimate use cases for prediction markets, such as forecasting and hedging. And we’re not here to stop anyone from trading event contracts for entertainment with extra money. We just don’t want these markets so easily conflated with the legitimate investing vehicles these apps already offer. And our reviews will reflect that.
