#3013. UnitedHealth Just Raised Guidance for the Third Time This Year. Where Will the Stock Be in 3 Years?

The health insurer's turnaround is lifting earnings. Here's what annual growth between 13% and 16% could mean for its stock by 2029.

UnitedHealth Group (UNH +1.89%) has raised its full-year earnings guidance for the third time this year as its turnaround gains momentum. And after a challenging stretch, its latest earnings report on Oct. 13 gave investors more reasons to be optimistic.

Now, with earnings showing signs of recovery, here's a look at where UnitedHealth could be over the next three years.

For much of the past two years, UnitedHealth Group has been dealing with operational setbacks, rising medical costs, and pressure on its Medicare Advantage business. But these days, it is beginning to show signs of a meaningful turnaround.

The clearest proof is its improving earnings outlook. When management initially issued its 2026 forecast in January, it expected adjusted earnings per share (EPS) of at least $17.75. That figure was raised to more than $18.25 following its first-quarter results, then increased to between $19.50 and $20 after the second quarter.

Then, in October, management raised its outlook for the third time this year, setting its adjusted EPS target to at least $20.50. More importantly, the upward revisions came alongside stronger operating performance, suggesting the company is making real improvements in its business.

Behind those gains, it has been working to simplify its operations, strengthen its leadership team, and refocus on its core U.S. healthcare business. The company has also been exiting certain international businesses, while making changes to its operating structure.

These moves suggest that management is focusing on areas where the company has stronger competitive advantages and better opportunities. Plus, UnitedHealth has another major advantage beyond its insurance operations.

Optum, the company's healthcare services and technology business, provides exposure to several areas of the industry. That includes pharmacy services, healthcare technology, and direct patient care. This diversification is important because it gives the company more ways to generate earnings beyond collecting insurance premiums.

Here's how it has shown up in the numbers. In the third quarter, Optum Health generated $735 million in operating earnings, compared with just $41 million in the same period last year. That translated to its operating margin improving to 3.2% from 0.2%, reflecting better medical cost management.

Optum Insight is another area worth watching as the business provides technology, analytics, and administrative solutions to healthcare providers and insurers. In fact, its artificial intelligence (AI) enabled products could become a strong growth driver as healthcare organizations seek to improve efficiency. Management said it remained on track to invest nearly $1.5 billion in AI-related initiatives in 2026, with applications aimed at improving productivity and making healthcare easier to navigate.

Looking ahead, with its turnaround gaining traction, the question is how much earnings growth it can deliver through 2029.

Management said its 2027 earnings growth target starts at the lower end of its longer-term target range of 13% to 16%. From there, assuming a 2026 adjusted EPS of $20.50 based on the company's latest guidance, these growth targets could lift it to between about $29.60 and $32 by 2029. Shares closed Nov. 9 at $397.62, a forward price-to-earnings ratio (P/E) of about 17.

In a more conservative scenario, UnitedHealth could reach around $444 per share, assuming a 15 P/E multiple. That reflects 13% annual growth, or $29.60 in adjusted EPS, and implies roughly 12% upside.

Meanwhile, the base case puts the stock at $554, using an 18 multiple. It reflects 14.5% annual growth, or $30.80 in adjusted EPS, and implies roughly 40% upside. The 18 multiple roughly matches today's forward P/E ratio.

Lastly, if the company's initiatives exceed expectations, a 21 multiple could push shares to around $672, reflecting 16% annual growth, or $32 in adjusted EPS, implying roughly 70% upside.

Despite the improving outlook, it still faces regulatory scrutiny, including investigations into its Medicare Advantage practices. The company is also exposed to rising medical costs and changes in government reimbursement.

Even so, UnitedHealth is clearly making progress, and its third guidance increase this year suggests its turnaround is accelerating. The next three years could be rewarding for investors if earnings continue to climb and the company delivers on its plans.

#3005. What we learned as Domantas Sabonis has uncharacteristic game in Kings' loss

What we learned as Domantas Sabonis has uncharacteristic game in Kings' loss originally appeared on NBC Sports Bay Area

SACRAMENTO — The Kings still search for their first home win of the 2026-27 NBA season after falling to the Orlando Magic by a final score of 107-100 on Tuesday night at Golden 1 Center.

The Magic, even without their best player as Paolo Banchero remains sidelined with a right ankle sprain, picked up just their third win of the season against Sacramento.

As we've seen far too often this season, the Kings' slow start to the game wound up haunting them. Sacramento turned the ball over eight times in the first quarter, resulting in 15 of the Magic's 34 points.

The Kings responded with an 18-0 run through the second quarter, but the Magic never let up and fought all the way back to regain the lead and maintain it until the final buzzer.

Zach LaVine led the way for the Kings with 31 points on 10-of-16 shooting and 6 of 9 from 3-point range, with three rebounds, two assists and two steals, but five turnovers in 33 minutes.

Kings rookie Darius Acuff Jr. trailed just behind him with 29 points on 10-of-21 shooting from the field and 4 of 9 from downtown, with four rebounds, six assists, two steals and four turnovers in 40 minutes.

Keegan Murray came off the bench for the second consecutive game after returning from an ankle injury. He finished with 11 points on 4-of-9 shooting, with two rebounds, one assist and two turnovers in 24 minutes.

Malik Monk played just three minutes off the bench. Rookie guard Emanuel Sharp played 19.

Precious Achiuwa started for the Kings but left the game early and didn't return with a leg contusion. LaVine also went to the locker room after rolling his ankle but returned.

The Kings, who dropped to 1-10 on the season, continue their seven-game homestand against the Portland Trail Blazers on Friday, when they will continue their search for their first home victory.

Here are the takeaways from the Kings' loss:

Darius Acuff Jr. entered Tuesday's game leading the NBA in minutes played per game at just above 37.

Coach Doug Christie was asked about it pregame, and he admitted Acuff's minutes should be "a tick" under where they currently are, but said he enjoys watching him play and seeing him on the floor.

On Tuesday, Acuff played 40 minutes, finishing with 29 points on 10-of-21 shooting from the field and 4 of 9 from downtown, with four rebounds, six assists, two steals and four turnovers.

The rookie really has become one of the few consistent bright spots for the Kings this season.

After a rocky start to this game, the Kings got going a bit toward the end of the first quarter.

The momentum continued into the second quarter, as Sacramento's offense came alive with an 18-0 run that began with Keegan Murray's first 3-pointer of the season.

Zach LaVine was a massive part of that run — on both ends of the floor. He had 13 points in that stretch before being substituted out of the game.

Orlando went on a run of its own with LaVine on the bench, responding with an 8-0 run to get right back in this game and eventually regain the lead.

LaVine was thrown back into the game after about two minutes of rest on the bench.

After scoring four points in the opening quarter, LaVine dropped 11 points in the second. He was plus-8 in the first half in plus/minus rating, while every other Kings starter was minus-7 or minus-8.

After a brief injury scare, LaVine finished with a team-high 31 points on 10-of-16 shooting and 6 of 9 from 3-point range, with three rebounds, two assists, two steals and five turnovers in 33 minutes.

Sabonis returned to action Tuesday after missing Sunday's game against the Miami Heat with left knee soreness.

But it was an unusual showing from the double-double machine.

He went three quarters without attempting a single shot, and his first attempt came from beyond the arc after 22 minutes of playing time. That isn't entirely shocking, as Sabonis is averaging just 9.0 field-goal attempts this season.

But what was a bit more concerning were his rebound numbers.

Sabonis, who is averaging an impressive 14.6 rebounds per game this season and nearly 11 throughout his 11-year NBA career, had just two rebounds on Tuesday.

He finished with zero points, two rebounds and five assists in 24 minutes.

Perhaps his knee still was bothering him, but nonetheless, it was an uncharacteristic showing from the rebounding machine.

#2998. Grocery Outlet: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors

Slowing new store openings in favor of infill sites is a bet that the company can grow profitably without leaning on promotions.

On its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Nov. 10, 2026, Grocery Outlet (GO +1.08%) announced a return to positive comparable store sales, which measure sales at stores open at least a year. The discount grocer is refocusing on its core model of buying deeply discounted surplus inventory to draw budget-conscious shoppers. Three things management said stand out for long-term investors.

Management phased out synthetic broad promotions and refocused on buying surplus brand-name products at deep discounts. That shift expanded customer visits to stores as inflation continued to squeeze household budgets.

After applying a targeted playbook to revitalize surplus grocery items, management repeated the process in frozen and deli. Replacing standard items with higher-margin opportunistic inventory accelerated sales growth across both departments.

To improve returns on capital expenditure, which means money spent on building stores, management is slowing store openings and prioritizing infill sites. Building within existing markets provides predictable returns and lowers execution risks.

Sales momentum accelerated entering the fourth quarter as customer traffic offset smaller basket sizes. Management is monitoring freight costs and maintenance expenses while leaning into established store footprints.

Management expects gross margins to expand year over year as higher-margin surplus deals replace artificial promotions. Capital allocation discipline will guide store expansion and supply chain efficiency into 2027.

#2997. Here's What $1,000 Invested in SpaceX Could Be Worth by the End of 2027

SpaceX's situation for the medium term looks complicated, to say the least.

In this inflation-riddled economy, $1,000 might not seem like a lot. But if that money is invested in the right company at the right time, it could create a foundation for life-changing returns over the long haul. Many investors are curious whether Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX +0.72%) has what it takes to go the distance after its record-setting $1.77 trillion initial public offering in June.

SpaceX has a lot going for it. CEO Elon Musk is no stranger to innovation and proving his naysayers wrong. And the company's spectacular recent results suggest he hasn't lost his Midas touch.

That said, the company still faces significant uncertainty, especially considering its sky-high valuation and the changing political climate after the Democrats swept the midterm elections. So what might a $1,000 investment might be worth by the end of next year?

Usually, large companies offer investors relative stability at the expense of high growth. But SpaceX flips this dynamic on its head. The space and artificial intelligence giant is growing like a weed, with third-quarter revenues soaring by 161% year over year to $14.1 billion, driven by the company's artificial intelligence segment, where revenues rose 830%. The AI segment, which SpaceX now calls its "super intelligence" unit, makes most of its money by accumulating data center hardware and renting out compute to clients that need to run and train large language models (LLMs).

The company has secured several deals with major AI companies like Anthropic and Alphabet, which is paying SpaceX a whopping $920 million per month for access to AI compute capacity. That said, it's difficult to know how long these types of deals will last, because many of SpaceX's clients have an incentive to invest in building their own data centers (and designing their own chips) rather than relying on third-party solutions. And most of the deals can be cancelled with a few months notice by either party.

SpaceX's management seems to be aware of that problem, and the company aims to bolster its moat by deploying a constellation of data center satellites in Earth orbit. If the technology works, it could offer significant advantages over ground-based compute due to abundant and essentially free solar energy, easier cooling, and perhaps less regulatory pushback. That last point may be more important than ever considering recent political developments.

While most business leaders avoid partisan politics to avoid the risk of potential brand damage, Musk has taken a different approach. He went all-in for Republicans and President Donald Trump in both 2024 and again in the 2026 U.S. midterm election, when he spent $474 million to support GOP candidates, including a whopping $224 million in Texas alone, where SpaceX has its headquarters, as well as significant launch and manufacturing facilities.

Musk's campaign contributions are constitutionally protected free speech. However, investors would be naive to assume that his actions can't have negative consequences for his companies.

Every Musk-backed Republican lost their election. Meanwhile, the Democrats are promising to impose more regulations on data center construction, which could slow the pace of AI expansion and drive up costs. On the other side of the business, SpaceX's Texas launch operations have already faced significant pressure from environmental groups. These headwinds are likely to increase over the coming years.

While SpaceX is a rapidly growing business, it faces substantial challenges from political uncertainty. And trading at a price-to-sales multiple of 55 (compared to the S&P 500's average ratio of just 3.6), its speculative valuation doesn't leave much room for error.

The potential for a mega-merger with Musk's other public company, Tesla, could make the problem even worse by saddling the combined company with a stagnating electric vehicle business.

With all this in mind, I don't see an investment in SpaceX growing substantially over the next 14 months. A $1,000 position opened today will probably still be worth around $1,000 in a base case scenario.

#2996. Game Preview: Phoenix aims to bounce back vs. Clippers

Who: Phoenix Suns (3-6) vs. Los Angeles Clippers (2-7)

Where: Mortgage Matchup Center — Phoenix, Arizona

The Phoenix Suns will need to have a short memory after being dominated by Victor Wembanyama and the Spurs last night.

Wemby walked into our building and dropped 40, 11, and nine blocks in 25 minutes without breaking a sweat. Spurs 122, Suns 96. It was a rough night. But the silver lining is that the starters were on the bench with 9:34 left. Because tonight they have the second of a back-to-back, and tired legs cannot be an excuse.

The mood in this fanbase right now is somewhere between "burn it down" and "it's November, relax." The Suns sit at 3-6. They're 2-2 on this seven-game homestand. The two-game win streak over Houston and Orlando either becomes a distant memory (after a loss) or a building block if they win, because then it's suddenly "they've won 3 of their last 4 games". So which is it?

Make no mistake about it… this is a MUST-WIN game for the Suns. These are the teams you need to beat.

Ingram and Beal are still out, so expect LA to run back the same five that started Sunday in their win over the Pelicans.

Mark Williams — OUT (Left Shoulder Surgery)

Devin Booker needs help, and he needs it from the starters.

Book went 10-for-17 for 32 last night. The other four starters combined for 27 points on 10-of-36 shooting. That's 27.8%. Phoenix shot 39.3% as a team. Jalen Green, Dillon Brooks and Miles Bridges have to be the second and third options tonight, or this turns into another Booker solo show that ends in a loss.

LA snapped a seven-game skid Sunday by beating New Orleans 139-123, and the bench won that game: 59 points and 14 assists from the reserves. Gradey Dick went 6-for-7. Top-5 pick Keaton Wagler hit 3 of 4 from deep in 18 minutes. Wagler also picked up five fouls. That unit is 4th in bench scoring per game, but defensively they have some flaws. Attack, attack, attack.

Darius Garland went for 24 and 10 against the Pelicans. Brook Lopez added 20. Brandon Ingram (heel) and Bradley Beal (knee) are both out tonight. Gillespie, Goodwin and Green have to make Garland work on the ball, and whoever draws Lopez has to drag him out to the perimeter, where his feet are slow.

Rebounding is going to be the key for every Suns game, as the Spurs outrebounded them by twenty, 55 to 35.

LA shot 55% from the field (46 of 84), went 16-for-38 from three, and piled up 34 assists against 11 turnovers in their win over the Pelicans. They lived at the line, too: 31 of 38 from the line while the Pelicans committed 29 fouls. The glass was basically even, 36-35 Clippers, with LA grabbing 13 offensive boards.

The starters held serve, every one of them finishing between +2 and +9. The bench blew it open. Max Strus and Gradey Dick were both +17, Kobe Sanders was +15, and Keaton Wagler was +11. LA won the fourth quarter 37-28.

Collin Gillespie, anyone? It's been a rough season for him, and boy could they use a breakout game in this one from him, not only for his confidence, but to outduel the Clippers' bench. Jordan Goodwin is back as well, so that hopefully provides a spark.

Do not take them lightly. The Clippers are 2nd in the NBA in 3PT% and 4th in bench scoring. Despite their flaws and 7-game losing streak, they are fully capable of getting hot from deep and stealing this one.

The Suns bounce back, and their offense breaks out in a win over the Clippers. We enter the 10-game mark at 4-6, with mixed reviews, but ultimately trending in the right direction, winning 3 of 4.

#2995. Coinbase Global vs. Toast: Which Financial Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?

Coinbase's crypto exchange and Toast's restaurant software are growing fast, but their valuations tell very different stories for investors.

Choosing between Coinbase Global (COIN -2.92%) and Toast (TOST -0.72%) requires pitting high-growth digital assets against the steady digitization of the restaurant industry. Which path leads to better long-term portfolio growth for investors today?

Coinbase Global operates as a primary bridge between traditional finance and the crypto economy. Toast provides a comprehensive technology stack that manages everything from point-of-sale to payroll for restaurants. Both companies represent the shift toward digital-first financial services, making them frequent candidates for growth-oriented investors looking toward 2027 and beyond.

Coinbase Global generates revenue by facilitating the exchange of digital assets for retail and institutional clients. The company also offers subscription and services revenue through its partnership with Circle (CRCL -3.82%) for the creation and redemption of the USDC (USDC +0.01%) stablecoin. By providing secure storage and developer tools, it aims to be the primary gateway for the crypto economy.

In its latest annual report for fiscal 2025, revenue reached nearly $7.2 billion, representing growth of approximately 9.4% over the prior period. The company reported net income of close to $1.3 billion, resulting in a net margin of roughly 17.6%. This net margin reflects the portion of total revenue remaining as profit after all expenses are paid.

As of Coinbase's December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio, which compares total debt to shareholder equity to assess financial leverage, is approximately 0.5. The current ratio, which measures liquidity, is nearly 2.3, while free cash flow reached close to $2.4 billion in fiscal 2025. Note that stock-based compensation accounted for roughly 34.6% of operating cash flow, inflating reported cash generation, since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

Toast provides an integrated platform that serves as the operating system for the restaurant industry. The company offers software, payment processing hardware, and financial services to more than 170,000 locations. It often partners with third parties, such as Amazon (AMZN +1.48%), to maintain its cloud infrastructure and deliver services to small and medium-sized businesses. This is a common strategy among tech stocks that focus on vertical software solutions.

In its latest annual report for fiscal 2025, Toast reported revenue of nearly $6.2 billion, a growth rate of approximately 24.1%. The company achieved net income of close to $342 million, a significant swing from its historical performance. This resulted in a net margin of roughly 5.6% for the year.

Toast's balance sheet as of December 2025 shows a debt-to-equity ratio of 0. The current ratio is approximately 2.8, and free cash flow for fiscal 2025 was nearly $608 million. Note that stock-based compensation represented roughly 36.6% of operating cash flow.

Coinbase Global faces significant revenue concentration in Bitcoin (BTC -0.11%) and Ethereum (ETH -0.74%) trading, making its results highly sensitive to price volatility. The company is also navigating intensive regulatory scrutiny, including investigations by the New York Attorney General regarding marketing practices. Furthermore, operational risks like cybersecurity threats and platform outages could affect its brand and financial stability.

Toast carries risks related to its reliance on a single bank partner for its working capital loan programs. A lawsuit from the FTC alleging deceptive pricing practices also poses a threat to its reputation and bottom line. Additionally, the company is concentrated in the small business restaurant market, which is vulnerable to inflation and broader economic downturns. Toast also relies on Amazon for platform hosting, creating a dependency on the stability of third-party services.

Toast appears cheaper based on its forward P/E and P/S ratio. These reflect future earnings estimates and sales over the past 12 months.

Valuation metrics include sourcing from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from other data providers.

Coinbase Global starts at a disadvantage here because I am a crypto skeptic. Crypto has no inherent value -- it doesn't produce earnings or cash flow and has no real-world utility. Buying cryptocurrency as an investment is entirely a bet that someone will later buy it from you at a higher price.

Furthermore, Coinbase Global's fortunes are inseparable from those of crypto:

Look at how closely Coinbase's stock mimics the price movements of Bitcoin and Ethereum (except worse). To me, Coinbase seems like a second-order play on crypto, and not a very good one, to boot.

Toast has a more reasonable valuation and also recently flipped from reporting a loss to a profit. Its POS systems are ubiquitous in the restaurant industry; it feels like every restaurant either runs on Toast or Square nowadays. I don't think crypto is a legitimate investment, and Coinbase is inextricably linked to the crypto market. Toast gets my vote here.

#2987. Standard Chartered Sees 50x Gains Ahead for This Surging Crypto. Here's Why It Could Be Worth a Closer Look.

This under-the-radar cryptocurrency could be one way to get exposure to the asset tokenization trend.

Real-world asset (RWA) tokenization remains one of the fastest-growing market opportunities within the crypto industry. In turn, this rapid growth is opening up all sorts of new investment options for investors.

One of the most promising options is Arbitrum (ARB -2.98%), a cryptocurrency that launched in 2021. It's growing by leaps and bounds right now, and Standard Chartered predicts it will soar to $10 by 2030. Based on its current price of approximately $0.20, there's the potential for an eye-popping 50x gain.

The tokenized asset market is currently worth $340 billion, but Standard Chartered sees this number ballooning to $4 trillion by 2030. There will be a massive land grab, as traditional finance firms rush to bring their financial assets on-chain.

And that's where Arbitrum enters the picture. Standard Chartered is calling it "the blockchain for TradFi (traditional finance)" for good reason. Wall Street firms and financial institutions that want to bring traditional financial assets (such as stocks and bonds) on-chain will turn to Arbitrum, a Layer-2 blockchain built on Ethereum.

The good news here is that Arbitrum collects 10% of net protocol revenue. So the more firms that sign up for real-world asset tokenization initiatives, the more money it will collect. We've already seen this dynamic in action with Robinhood Markets, which recently launched Robinhood Chain in partnership with Arbitrum.

The launch of Robinhood Chain immediately led to a surge in transaction volume, and Arbitrum has been making money hand over fist as a result. In September alone, Arbitrum pocketed more than $5 million in fees. It's gotten to the point where some investors are now talking about the "Robinhood Chain Effect." Other finance firms could follow Robinhood's lead, creating even more revenue opportunities for Arbitrum.

This might sound like a fantastic business model, but a lot can still go wrong. For example, the pace of real-world asset tokenization may cool off, which will directly impact Arbitrum's future growth prospects.

Moreover, Arbitrum has plenty of potential rivals. Its nearest competitor is Base, the Layer-2 blockchain from Coinbase Global. So it's not like Arbitrum has a monopoly on real-world asset tokenization.

Finally, it's still unclear whether investors prefer investing in Layer-1 blockchains, such as Ethereum, or in Layer-2 blockchains, such as Arbitrum. Currently, all the value is flowing to Layer-2 blockchains, but that could change.

Investors can pick up ARB at an unbelievable 92% discount to its all-time high of $2.40. Even if Arbitrum doesn't reach $10 by 2030, it could still deliver 10x gains by reclaiming the $2 price level. That type of upside potential should make Arbitrum worth a closer look heading into 2027.

#2985. Boston Celtics (8-2) at Philadelphia 76ers (9-2) Game #11 11/10/26

Boston Celtics (8-2) at Philadelphia 76ers (9-2)Tuesday, November 10, 20268:00 PM ETGame #11 Road #6TV: Peacock/NBCRadio: 98.5 The Sports Hub, 97.5 The Fanatic, Sirius XMXfinity Mobile Arena

The Celtics visit the Philadelphia 76ers for the first of 4 games between them this season. They will meet in Philadelphia again on February 7. They will meet twice in Boston on January 21 and March 7. This is likely the most anticipated matchup of the season so far as there are many stories to watch in this game.

First, there is the beef, or the lamb chops and gravy, or whatever you want to call what has been going on between Jayson Tatum and Jaylen Brown since the trade. In the preseason, as they were both warming up, they didn't even acknowledge each other. There has been a back and forth of words between them ever since. Also there is the story of Paul George returning to Philly for the first time and of Jaylen Brown and PG13 facing their former teams. There is also the story of the long time rivalry between the Celtics and 76ers and the teams who faced each other in the 2nd round of the playoffs last season.

There is also the story of the top 2 teams in the East facing off. The 8-2 Celtics are 2nd in the East with only Philadelphia (9-2) half a game ahead of them in the standings. The Celtics have won their last 3 games and the 76ers are looking for their 2nd straight win. The Celtics are 2-2 on the road while the 76ers are 4-2 at home. The Celtics won both games in the preseason. Both teams are 2-0 in games against division rivals.

The Celtics are playing in the first of back to back games. This is their 3rd back to back set this season already. They won the first game in both of their back to back sets this season. One win was at home while the other was on the road. The Celtics are 275-200 overall all time against the 76ers. They are 94-130 in games played in Philly. They tied the series 2-2 last season, with each team winning one at home and one on the road.

The 76ers made one of the biggest moves of the off season, trading Paul George to the Celtics to get Jaylen Brown. They also signed LeBron James, Dean Wade, Ariel Hukporti and Anfernee Simons as free agents. They drafted Labaron Philon, Jr with the 22nd pick in the draft. Along with Paul George, they lost Quentin Grimes, Kelly Oubre, Jr and Andre Drummond. Mike Gansey also replaced Daryl Morey as the 76ers' president of basketball operations.

After this game, the Celtics will complete their 4 game road trip with a game in Toronto in back to back games Wednesday. Then they play Dallas and Orlando at home before a West coast trip that takes them through Denver, Sacramento, Golden State, and Washington. They then play one game at home against Atlanta before playing at San Antonio and Dallas. Then it's home against Charlotte before a game at Brooklyn.

The 76ers will host Toronto and Indiana before road games at Brooklyn and Orlando. Then they host Milwaukee, Portland and Miami before games at Indiana and Houston. Then they have a 3 game home stand against Memphis, Denver and Orlando before playing at Orlando. Next they host Dallas and play at Charlotte. They will host Houston before a 5 game Western road trip.

The Celtics have been changing their starting lineup with Jordan Walsh, Hugo Gonzalez, Baylor Scheierman, and Neemias Queta getting starts along with Derrick White, Paul George, Jayson Tatum and Mitchell Robinson. The starting lineup is a work in progress for the Celtics, especially the shooting guard spot that has changed pretty much from game to game. Mike Conley got the start against the Bucks, but I'm guessing that White, Walsh, George, Tatum and Queta get the start in this one. The 76ers should start Maxey, Edgecombe, Brown, James and Embiid.

The Celtics have no one on the injury report as of this time. Chris Cenac, Jr and the Celtics 3 two way players will likely be with Maine. The 76ers have 3 players out as of now. Adem Bona and Dominick Barlow are both out due to back injuries. Ariel Hukporti is out for the season due to a torn Achilles. Joel Embiid has been struggling with plantar faciitis but is expected to play in this game.

Probable Starting MatchupsPG: Derrick White vs Tyrese Maxey

Celtics ReservesChris Cenac, JrMike Conley, JrLuka GarzaJordan WalshRon Harper, JrSam HauserPayton PritchardMitchell RobinsonBaylor Scheierman

Two Way PlayersDevin CarterDillon MitchellAmari Williams

76ers ReservesAnfernee SimonsDean WadeKentavious Caldwell-PopeJabari WalkerJustin EdwardsLebaron Philon, Jr,

2-Way PlayersTaco FallRayan RupertCaleb Love

Injuries/OutAdem Bona (back) outDominick Barlow (back) outAriel Hukporti (Achilles) out

Key MatchupsDerrick White vs Tyrese MaxeyMaxey is averaging 26.9 points, 3.7 rebounds, 5.5 assists, and 1.4 steals per game. He is shooting 48.1% from the field and 34.1% from beyond the arc. His 26.9 ppg ranks 3rd in the East. He is quick and so the Celtics will need to work hard to stay in front of him. They will need Derrick White's defense to be sharp in this one.

Paul George vs Jaylen BrownThis should be an incredible matchup to watch. Brown is averaging 22.3 points, 6.7 rebounds, 4.0 assists, and 1.2 steals. He is shooting 47.7% from the field and 39.2% from beyond the arc. I expect Brown to come in with a chip on his shoulder to prove that he is the better player among Paul George, Jayson Tatum and himself. Paul George just needs to focus on playing team ball and being his best self.

Honorable MentionNeemias Queta vs Joel EmbiidEmbiid is averaging 17.9 points, 9.7 rebounds, and 4.1 assists per game. He is shooting 38% from the field and 10% from beyond the arc. The Celtics need to keep Embiid out of the paint and off the boards. Queta needs to find a way to stay out of foul trouble and to counter Embiid on defense.

Keys to the GameDefense – As always, defense is absolutely the key to winning this, and every, game. It is very true that defense wins championships. Shots don't always fall but players can always play hard on defense. The Celtics are 3rd with an offensive rating of 117.9 while the 76ers are 20th with an offensive rating of 110.3. The Celtics are 4th with a defensive rating of 106.3. The 76ers aren't far behind with a defensive rating of 107.6. The Celtics must give full out effort on defense for every minute of this game if they hope to beat the loaded 76ers team.

Rebound – Next to defense, rebounding is always a big key to winning. The key to rebounding is effort and focus. The 76ers are 19th with 43.4 rebounds per game while the Celtics are 10th with 45.0 rebounds per game. The Celtics have to fight as a team to try to grab every rebound to avoid the 76ers getting 2nd chance points because the 76ers average 14.7 second chance points per game. In order to win the possession battle, the Celtics must crash the boards and fight for every rebound.

Effort and Focus for 48 Minutes – The Celtics have to play with extra effort overall for all 4 quarters. They have to stay focused on playing basketball the right way as a team. They have to avoid getting wound up in the Tatum vs Brown and Brown vs George narratives. They have to play team ball and give all out effort to get to the basket, to defend, to rebound, to hustle after loose balls and to play hard on every possession.

Move the Ball Carefully – The Celtics play the best when they move the ball and find the best shot. They struggle when they try to do too much individually. But, they have to be careful handling the ball and making passes. The 76ers are best in the league at taking care of the ball with just 12.9 turnovers per game. The Celtics are 12th with 14.9 turnovers per game. They have to stay focused and avoid turning the ball over.

X-FactorsOn the Road – The Celtics will be on the road once again for the 3rd straight game and they will be facing a very hostile crowd. Philly fans hate the Celtics because they have pretty much owned them in recent years. They hate Jayson Tatum because the Celtics took him with Philly's pick after the 76ers traded up to take Markelle Fultz. They now have another reason to hate the Celtics and that is to back up Jaylen Brown who has been very bitter against the Celtics and his former running mate. There will likely be a lot of boos and the Celtics need to play through them. They have to shake off the distractions of playing on the road and stay focused on playing Celtics basketball.. They can use the boos as motivation to play even harder.

Coaching – Joe Mazzulla is in his 5th season as Celtics' head coach. He won a title in 2024 with a very talented team that was packed with shooting stars. Now he has to win in a different way since his personnel has changed and so far he is doing a good job. Nick Nurse is in his 9th season as a head coach overall and his 4th as the 76ers head coach. He won a title with the Raptors in 2019. Nurse came out ahead in the playoffs last season. Can Mazzulla win this round?

Officiating – Officiating is always an x-factor in every game. Every crew officiates differently. Some call it tight, others let them play. The Celtics need to adjust to how the refs are calling the game and not allow bad calls or no calls to take away their focus from playing the game. The Celtics also have to be aware of the new points of emphasis for this season and try to avoid flopping, off‑arm push‑offs, reckless closeouts, delays before free throws, and illegal screens. They have been especially calling flops and push offs and so the Celtics need to make an effort to avoid doing both.

#2983. StubHub: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors

Rapid deleveraging cut net leverage from 4.5 to 2.5 times EBITDA, but the open distribution push is still unproven at scale.

On its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Nov. 10, 2026, StubHub (STUB -3.42%) announced an increase in its full-year gross merchandise sales, representing the total dollar value of tickets sold on its platform, guidance to 11% to 13% growth. Operating efficiency drove adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) margin up 10 percentage points year over year to 25%. Debt repayments of $1.1 billion since its initial public offering have lowered borrowing costs and strengthened its balance sheet. Three takeaways from management's comments stand out.

Sales and marketing costs fell nine percentage points year over year to 45% of revenue in the third quarter. Management attributes this efficiency to established market leadership, allowing it to capture repeat customer traffic without spending heavily on acquiring buyers.

Net leverage dropped from 4.5 times adjusted EBITDA at the end of 2025 to 2.5 times at the end of the third quarter of 2026. The company paid down $100 million of debt in July and extended term loan maturities to October 2033, creating balance sheet flexibility for strategic investments.

Management is expanding beyond traditional resale through open distribution, which allows primary ticket sellers and content owners to list inventory directly on the platform without exclusivity. Concurrently, the platform is testing sponsored listings, allowing sellers to pay for elevated visibility as event dates approach.

Live event demand remains steady across sports and music categories, and international concert travel continues to expand the customer base. StubHub benefits from network effects and a long operational history handling high-demand ticket fulfillment, while management watches the timing of major 2027 concert ticket releases and updates to search engine algorithms.

With leverage down and term loan maturities pushed out to October 2033, the company is shifting focus toward driving free cash flow per share over the long term.

Global stock markets have been volatile as investors assess high bond yields and continued tensions between the U.S. and Iran. There are concerns about the impact of uncertainty in the Middle East on oil prices and consequently on inflation.

Investors who prefer to look beyond short-term noise and buy stocks with attractive long-term growth potential can follow the recommendations of top Wall Street analysts. The ratings of these experts are backed by in-depth research of a company's financials and thorough analysis of the factors affecting its business performance.

Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

Semiconductor giant Nvidia (NVDA) reported stellar fiscal second-quarter results and reassured investors about continued strength in AI-driven demand for its chips. Moreover, Nvidia's FY28 revenue growth outlook of 70% was well above the Street's expectations.

Reacting to the Q2 print, Morgan Stanley analyst Joseph Moore reiterated a buy rating on NVDA and increased his price target to $300 from $288. "This is our Top Pick in the semis group, with a compelling product cycle, exceptional growth and valuation below peers," said the 5-star analyst.

Nvidia delivered impressive quarterly results despite supply constraints, Moore said, but he believes that the FY28 revenue and gross margin commentary mattered more, with a favorable outlook for both measures.

Moore said Nvidia's 70% revenue growth guidance for FY28 was above his own estimate of 52% and the consensus of about 40%. The top-line growth estimate was a "remarkable figure" given supply issues and Moore said he expects Nvidia to continue to address bottlenecks to deliver rapid growth.

Among other takeaways, the analyst said performance metrics for Vera Rubin chips were strong, with Nvidia emphasizing a 30x higher throughput per megawatt and 35x lower token cost compared with Grace Blackwell Ultra.

Moore ranks No. 159 among more than 12,490 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 60% of the time, delivering an average return of 24.60%. See Nvidia Statistics on TipRanks.

Ride-hailing and delivery platform Uber Technologies (UBER) was recommended by BMO Capital analyst Brian Pitz, who discussed the company's opportunity in the autonomous vehicle (AV) market in a recent research note that reiterated a buy rating and price target of $119.

The 5-star analyst highlighted Uber's transition into a diversified marketplace, with investors now focusing on its AV growth prospects. The key question is how much value can Uber generate as AVs become commercialized, Pitz asked.

"We continue to believe that Uber's AV strategy is evolving and will become a significant driver of revenue and profitability," the analyst said.

Importantly, Pitz believes that Uber can establish itself as a preferred mobility platform for AV makers, supported by its growing AV infrastructure capabilities and an expanding partner base. This would enable Uber to win a significant share of value as the AV market is commercialized.

Additionally, Pitz noted Uber's enhanced position in the AV value chain, with the company shifting from serving as a distribution channel for robotaxis to becoming a broader platform for AV mobility. The analyst discussed Uber's efforts to capture growth opportunities in the AV market, including higher capital spending, expansion into new markets and building partnerships beyond Alphabet's Waymo.

Pitz ranks No. 574 among more than 12,490 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 61% of the time, delivering an average return of about 12.20%. See Uber Technologies Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

Semiconductor company Marvell Technology (MRVL) recently announced better-than-expected results for the second quarter of FY27. But the company's increased FY28 guidance fell short of investors' high expectations.

In reaction to the Q2 FY27 results, KeyBanc analyst John Vinh reaffirmed a buy rating on Marvell Technology, with a price target of $400. The analyst noted that Marvell's results and outlook were driven by strength in its data center business. The Q2 FY27 data center business grew 46% year-over-year, to $2.17 billion, far above KeyBanc's estimate of $2.09 billion.

Management "highlighted accelerating AI networking demand across scale-out, scale-across and scale-up architectures, supported by strong 800G optical DSP demand, rapid 1.6T ramp, broader 51.2T switch deployments and higher TIA/driver demand," Vinh said.

Consequently, Marvell raised its data center revenue guidance, now expecting 60% growth in FY27 and more than 60% in FY28.

Regarding the recently announced $120 billion warrant arrangement with Google, Vinh said management argued that programs tied to the warrant are already priced into the custom outlook through FY28. Meanwhile, new programs and those in execution are expected to drive significant upside to the previous FY29 custom XPU revenue estimate of over $10 billion, Vinh said, citing management.

#2979. Darius Acuff Jr.‘s frustration level reaches new high after Kings' 1-10 start

Darius Acuff Jr.'s frustration level reaches new high after Kings' 1-10 start originally appeared on NBC Sports Bay Area

SACRAMENTO — The start of Darius Acuff's NBA career hasn't necessarily gone as he had hoped.

The Kings fell to 1-10 after losing to the Orlando Magic on Tuesday night and still search for their first home win of the season.

It took seven games for Acuff to get a taste of his first NBA victory when the Kings defeated the Dallas Mavericks over a week ago. The Kings had a chance to carry over the momentum as they returned to Sacramento to open a seven-game homestand at Golden 1 Center.

But they lost to the Los Angeles Lakers, San Antonio Spurs, Miami Heat and, most recently, the Magic, to begin this home stretch 0-4.

The Lakers and Spurs games were scheduled losses, but it seems like the Kings had every opportunity to walk away with wins against a struggling Heat team and a lowly Magic squad, or at the very least go 1-3 in that stretch.

Instead, the Kings are one of the three teams in the NBA already with 10 losses on the season.

"1-10 just don't sound right," Acuff said postgame.

Acuff, who is known for his even-keeled, cool, calm and collected persona, visibly was frustrated after Tuesday's loss.

So much so that he couldn't even find the words to explain what's gone wrong for the Kings so far this season. The 19-year-old was asked to identify the most frustrating part of these losses.

"When the clock says zero and we lost," he responded. "I don't understand. I don't know. I don't know what to do, man. I feel like we're trying. Everybody as a whole. We're just not coming out with the win. It's just, I don't know, man."

The emotions stem from Acuff's character and what he's used to. And that doesn't, and never has, included losing.

So this is foreign territory for a competitor like Acuff, who is making NBA history seemingly every night and joining the record books with basketball legends such as LeBron James and Michael Jordan, yet his only goal is to win games.

Eleven games into the season, all the losses already are taking a toll on the young point guard.

"A lot," he said when asked how much of a toll the 1-10 start is taking on him. "I'm not a loser, so it's not fun. But like I said, it's an 82-game season, so hopefully something will shake."

Acuff finished Tuesday's loss with 29 points on 10-of-21 shooting, with four rebounds, six assists, four turnovers and two steals in 40 minutes.

So far this season, Acuff is averaging 26.2 points, 3.8 rebounds and 7.3 assists in a league-high 37-plus minutes played per game.

It is early in the season, and the wins, although maybe not many, eventually will come for Acuff and the Kings. But after Tuesday's loss, the rookie seemed to be on the verge of tired of hearing that without anything changing.

"I mean, yeah, we've been saying that for five games now, so it's kind of hard to keep saying that without actually doing it," Acuff said. "We just got to go out there and actually do it. We're on the court playing. There's nobody playing but ourselves. Like I said, we just got to get better as a team. And to answer your question, it's just kind of the second half, it's kind of frustrating. It's like the first half we come out with energy, and then in the third quarter sometimes we don't, and then we do. And then the fourth quarter, the last five minutes of a game, we just can't put it together as a team.

"I think we're trying. We're talking as a staff, as a team. But like I said, when the clock hits zero, we just lose, and that's the most frustrating part."

The melancholy mood was the same when Zach LaVine approached the postgame podium. LaVine, who had five turnovers in Tuesday's loss, said he's "been in the league too damn long" to turn the ball over like he did.

But while LaVine also might have been disappointed with his team's start to the season, the 13-year veteran guard offered his own perspective on the current state of the struggling Kings.

"I mean, there's going to be outside people saying things. There's going to be a lot of finger-pointing," LaVine said. "I think, for us, we got to try to stay together from the front office down. We all have the same record right now, and it's us versus everybody else. So that's how we have to look at it. We have to try to figure out as a unit how are we going to, you know, start putting together more games where we can give ourselves a chance to win. We're trending in the right area.

"It feels a lot better out there. We've done a lot of better things, but we just got to clean up the small mistakes, myself included, to where we put together a full 48. I think then we get that satisfaction to where we win a game, and maybe we can start getting a couple more and more. The situation is what it is, but this is our job, and we have to figure out, at least as a vet myself, to keep guys uplifted, bring it each and every day, bring it in practice, regardless how you're feeling, I think that's just part of it. So I'm going to."

The irritation was apparent in the locker room, too, as most players already had left the arena by the time the media was let in.

De'Andre Hunter did speak in the locker room postgame, and his words immediately matched his demeanor when asked where the frustration level is at right now.

He also didn't sugarcoat his response when asked what the Kings need to clean up in order to turn a corner on the season.

"Everything," he said. "Just not good enough."

It isn't necessarily a surprise that the Kings aren't one of the top teams in the Western Conference, but this 1-10 start still feels worse than anyone could have imagined.

And judging by the players' mood postgame Tuesday, the frustration level has reached an all-time high.

There is the possibility that these built-up emotions turn into motivation that the Kings could use to start winning games. And at this point, that really is all they can lean on.

"That's all we have is motivation," Hunter said. "With losing, you can't really build any chemistry. No team camaraderie. But we just got motivation about the next game."
